action_summary: The Perfect Algorithm's scan took the set of possible actions as an ARGUMENT. On the project's five machines that set is a hand-written tuple of Atoms, per machine, by a person, so 'enter any new environment and ask the right question' had an unmeasured precondition: a human must first hand the loop the list of doors. The frontier fails on the same step -- Terminal-Bench 2.0 puts 'command not found' at 24.1% of every failure, an agent guessing what exists on a machine. This round removes the guess. Every program publishes a contract about itself in --help, and canonical/runtime/tool_census_v1 reads it and then RUNS each declared operation on a disposable tree that is restored afterwards, so the tree -- not a table of ours -- decides what each door really does. Measured on 36 programs present on this machine: 2,134 operations read from their own declarations, classified into 76 DOORS (ran clean and moved the tree, with the kind of move recorded), 1,098 SENSORS (ran clean, computed a value, moved nothing) and 960 UNBOUND (the program's own usage line says it cannot run as invoked), in 54 s with the tree restored exactly after every trial. The decisive proof: gzip's 12 doors were discovered by the census and perfect_algorithm_v1.scan(env, env.action_names) then walked that environment -- 5 states, 12 transitions, 0.028 s -- with action_list_written_by_a_person false. Six defects each made the census lie and each was caught by disbelieving a number: prose admitted as subcommands; a program answering with its own help admitted as a subcommand; an error message mistaken for a manual; one door counted per spelling; 958 of 998 'doors' produced by the retry loop reading its own seed write as the operation's effect; and a FAILED run's litter counted as a capability.

falsification_condition: The claim is false if a tool whose declaration is well-formed yields doors the tree does not confirm, or if a NO_EFFECT operation turns out to be a door under any constructible room, or if any trial leaves the tree altered. Each of those is a reported defect, not a tolerated one -- six such defects are recorded in the receipt.
honest_limits: This is not competence. Knowing 76 doors is not knowing which one a request wants; the census answers 'what can be done here', not 'what should be done'.
960 operations are UNCHARACTERISED, not dead. The census supplies what a usage line declares; a room with two files, a genuine patch, or a committed change is a stated decision it does not yet make.
git commit --all is knowingly mis-bound: git says 'paths with -a does not make sense' only in its ERROR, not its description, so the binder cannot read it without inventing a word list.
A room is a decision. git is judged inside a repository the census builds; changing which rooms exist changes the door count, so the room is stated per tool rather than hidden.
A GUI has no --help; that tier needs the accessibility tree or the DOM, and this sandbox has no display. man is also absent, so --help is the only declaration tier measured.
Producer-run sandbox only; no independent identity re-ran any of it; truth.achieved stays false.
